To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
photosynthesis is not inhibited by light pulses shorter than 100 μs, but is inhibited when pulses are longer than 2 ms.

photosynthesis in tomato leaves is not inhibited by pulses of light as short as 1.5 ms and is only slightly inhibited by pulses of 2 ms, and that zeaxanthin is formed in leaves when they dissipate light energy, but is not formed by pulsed irradiation.

1) the photon requirement of tomato leaves is 10.3, 2) the photon requirement is independent of the light source spectral quality and 3) pulsed light of 100 μm pulses can support photosynthesis as efficiently as continuous light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of pulsed light on photosynthesis and the xanthophyl cycle.
the effect of pulsed light on photosynthesis.
the efficiency of photosynthesis in light of different wavelengths, and the efficiency of photosynthetic utilization of pulsed light.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pulsed irradiation of photosynthetic tissue can be as efficient as continuous irradiation when the pulses are short enough to allow for storage of the absorbed photons in the reaction center.
photosynthesis in leaves of tomato is more sensitive to the duration of the light pulses and the dark periods than the total amount of light delivered.
the efficiency of photosynthesis was the highest when light was delivered in pulses of 1 ms or less and the lowest when light was delivered continuously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the photon requirement of the photosynthetic apparatus is 10.3 and that light pulses of less than 2 ms can be used to drive electron transport without the loss of energy that occurs in the formation of the xanthophylic cycle.
the light utilization efficiency of photosynthesis is the same whether the photons are provided continuously or in pulses of 1.5 ms or less.
photosynthesis is more efficient in pulsed light of 100 μsec duration or less, but that longer pulses are detrimental to photosynthetic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
light pulses can be used as a tool to investigate photosynthetic processes and to improve the efficiency of photosynthesis in LED lighting.
the efficiency of photosynthetic electron transport can be increased in plants by using pulsed light from LEDs.
the efficiency of photosynthesis is not affected by short pulses of light, but the efficiency of photosynthetic electron transport is affected by long pulses of light.
